claim: Lloyd Harry Houle's father was David Houle, born 1884 at Fort Ripley
where: AI-assisted research, 2025 and 2026, and the person notes built from it
correction: Lloyd appears in the 1930 census at Forest Lake as the thirteen year old son of John J. Houle, 38, and Lydia, 33. John J.'s own death record in 1970 names his parents as John A. Houle and Mathilda Letourneau. There is no David in this line.

claim: Honore Houle, Sarah Doucette, Genevieve Cartier and David Houle are direct ancestors
correction: Every one of them hung off David Houle, and with David out of the line Honore Houle, Sarah Doucette and David have no documented connection to this family. Genevieve Cartier is the exception: she turned out to be a direct ancestor after all, by a different route. She was Michel Houle's first wife and John Baptiste's mother, named in his 1842 baptism and in her own 1829 marriage. The line above Lloyd runs John Joseph, John A., John B., then Michel and Genevieve.

claim: Samuel Morkert, born 1839 in Parke County, Indiana, was DeAnn's second great-grandfather
correction: Archibald Monroe Morkert's father was Henry Newton Morkert, born 1851 in Indiana, named in the 1910 census household in Baldwin County, Alabama. Samuel has no documented place in this line.

claim: John Lewis Morkert and Catherine Kachelriess are third great-grandparents
correction: They were reached through Samuel, who is not in the line. The fourth great-grandparents are probably Elias Silas Morkert and Elizabeth Burkhalter of Carroll County, on the evidence of the 1880 census. That is a probable match, not a proof.

claim: The Morkerts settled in Parke and Fountain Counties, Indiana
correction: Morkerts were in Parke County, and an Elias Morkert appears there in the 1850 census. The documented direct line, though, is in Clay Township, Carroll County, where three Morkert households sit in the 1880 census.

claim: Michel Houle, a founding settler of Centerville, is an ancestor
correction: He is an ancestor, but not through David Houle. John B. Houle's 1929 death record names his father as Michael Houle, and John B. is Lloyd's great-grandfather. The claim survived the collapse of the path that produced it.

claim: Tyler and Olivia are Kenneth Morkert's children
where: Person notes in the Obsidian vault, May 2026
correction: Joe Morkert's 2003 obituary names four nieces and nephews: Tyler, Anna, Jazlyn and Olivia. Tyler is T.J. himself. Three of the four are DeAnn's, which leaves Olivia as Kenneth's. Kenneth has two children, Olivia and Dylan; Dylan is not in the 2003 list, so he was most likely born after it.

claim: The Morkerts went from Indiana straight to North Dakota
where: Every earlier account of the family
correction: The 1910 census places Henry, Mary and Archibald at Foley and Magnolia Springs in Baldwin County, Alabama. The route was Ohio, Indiana, Alabama, North Dakota, then Minnesota.

claim: Michel Houle's wife was Kadzi Tougon, probably Tougas, the mother of Thomas and possibly of John Baptiste
where: This site, from Thomas Houle's 1934 Minnesota death record
correction: Michel married twice. His first wife, Genevieve Cartier, was John Baptiste's mother (1842 baptism) and died in 1847. His second, Marie Lataille, married at Sainte-Victoire-de-Sorel, was Thomas's mother (1851 baptism) and died in 1854. Kadzi Tougon is the 1934 clerk's rendering of Marie Lataille, not a third woman, and the guess of Tougas is withdrawn.
